text: there is no such thing as a Biblical literalist hey everybody I'm Dan mclen I'm a scholar of the Bible and religion and I count at least three reasons you
cannot have biblical literalism the first is that the text of the Bible as a text has no inherent meaning meaning is
generated through a process of negotiation as readers engage the text in specific circumstances and those
readers and their specific circumstances are almost always going to take priority in that negotiation the text is is going
to be leveraged as the Authority for whatever reading is negotiated but the text is pretty much never going to
dictate precisely what comes out of the end of that negotiation and particularly if doing so would compromise the
interests or the power structures of the readers in their circumstances second reason is that the
text is not univocal it is inconsistent it frequently contradicts itself and so in that process of negotiation
the text is going to be smoothed out so that it is something that is livable by actual people operating in time and
space and that means that certain things in the text are going to be centered and prioritized and other things in the text are going to be marginalized suppressed
reinterpreted or outright ignored and whether people want to acknowledge that or not everyone who approaches the Bible
as an authoritative text has rejected marginalized suppressed ignored parts of the text that are uncomfortable to them
and their traditions and their needs and exigencies the third reason is that the text is phenomenally outdated there are
numerous parts of the text that are not meaningful or useful to us today which means that in that negotiation there are lots of things that we have jettisoned
many of these things were jettisoned long ago and people have had a long time to come up with ways to rationalize to
themselves why it's perfectly okay or even require re ired that they reject certain parts of the text even parts of
the text that are consistent throughout such as the endorsement of slavery such as the normativity of polygamy and
things like that we come up with ways to make ourselves okay with having ignored those things but that's really all that
is US deciding that we're the authority and we're going to come up with ways to be happy with our negotiation of the
biblical text so there is no biblical literalism there is literalism regarding tradition literalism regarding how we
structure power and values within and between groups there is literalism regarding the needs and interests of our identity politics but there is no such
thing as biblical literalism
